title: He had status.
paragraphs:
He had status.
He had influence.
He had a name people respected.
But none of that could keep his daughter alive.
So Jairus ran.

Not walked.
Not waited.
Ran.
And when he found Jesus, this ruler of the synagogue didn’t stand tall—he fell.
At His feet.
Begging.
“My little daughter is dying. Please come…” (Mark 5:23)
Feel that.
A father with nothing left to hold on to except hope in a Man others were still debating.

Because when death enters your house, titles don’t matter.
Money goes silent.
Reputation cannot heal.
Only Jesus.
And maybe that’s where you are right now.

Smiling outside.
Breaking inside.
Holding it together for everyone—while something you love is slipping away.
Jairus shows us something raw, something real:
Desperation is not weakness.
It is often the doorway to faith.
But here’s the tension we don’t talk about…

Jesus says yes.
He starts walking with Jairus.
Hope is rising.
Then suddenly—He stops.

A woman touches Him.
A miracle happens.
And Jairus… waits.
Can you imagine that moment?

Every second feels like betrayal.
Every delay feels dangerous.
Every breath is a countdown.
“Jesus, not now…”
But heaven’s timeline is not rushed by human panic.
And then it hits.
The message arrives like a knife:
“Your daughter is dead. Why trouble the Teacher any further?” (Mark 5:35)
That’s it.
That’s the sentence that buries hope.
Some of you have heard your own version of that line.

“It’s too late.”
“It’s over.”
“Nothing can change this now.”
But Jesus interrupts the funeral with one command:
“Do not fear, only believe.” (Mark 5:36)
Read that again.

He didn’t say, “Understand everything.”
He didn’t say, “Fix it.”
He said—believe.

Because faith is not built on your control.
It is built on His authority.

Jesus walks into a house full of noise, weeping, and finality.
People already accepted the ending.
But Jesus saw something they couldn’t.
He takes the girl by the hand.

“Talitha koum.”
“Little girl, I say to you, arise.” (Mark 5:41)
And just like that—
Death lets go.
Life returns.
Hope breathes again.
And the room that was drowning in grief becomes a witness to glory.
But don’t miss this…
This story is not just about Jairus’ daughter.
It’s about you.
Because spiritually, we were the ones lying there.

Unresponsive.
Hopeless.
Dead in sin. (Ephesians 2:1)

No effort could revive us.
No religion could wake us.
But Jesus stepped into our silence.

At the cross, He took our sin.
In the grave, He carried our death.
And through the resurrection, He crushed what was crushing us.
This is the Gospel:
We don’t clean ourselves up and come alive.
He calls us out of death.

By grace.
Through faith.
In Christ alone.

So when Jesus says, “Do not fear, only believe”—
He is not asking for blind optimism.
He is calling you to trust the One who has authority over death itself.

That situation you think is over?
That relationship you buried?
That part of you you gave up on?
Bring it to Him.

Not polished.
Not perfect.
But honest.
Because Jesus is not intimidated by dead ends.
He specializes in resurrection.
And maybe today, He’s not just coming to fix your situation.
Maybe He’s coming to awaken your faith.

To teach you that delay is not denial.
That silence is not absence.
That death is not the end when He is Lord.
So fall at His feet.
Like Jairus.

No mask.
No pride.
No pretending.
Just surrender.
And listen closely…
He is still saying it.

Over your fear.
Over your doubt.
Over your impossible:
Do not fear.
Only believe.
Because what Jesus touches—
Lives.
